 caret-right News | Israel-Palestine conflict Israeli air strike hits hospital, 13 killed across Gaza
 Attack on Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis kills six as the UN appeals for urgent aid to deal with heavy rains in Gaza. 
 Listen Listen (5 mins) Save
 Share Israeli air strike hits hospital, 13 killed across Gaza on social media share-nodes Share
 facebook x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Members of the Palestinian Civil Defence inspect damage inside a building at Nasser Medical Complex following an Israeli air strike in Khan Younis on November 12, 2026 [Reuters] By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters Published On 11 Nov 2026 11 Nov 2026 | Updated: 26 minutes ago Updated: 26 minutes ago Israeli attacks have killed at least 13 Palestinians across Gaza, as the United Nations made an emergency appeal for waterproof tents to shelter hundreds of thousands exposed to flooding due to heavy rains.
 At least six Palestinians were killed in an Israeli air strike on the Nasser Medical Complex west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, according to Gaza’s health ministry and civil defence. The attack in the early hours of Thursday wounded 20 other people.

 end of list “Most of those killed and injured were patients, including people who were scheduled to undergo surgery the following day,” said Al Jazeera’s Hind Khoudary, reporting from Gaza City.
 She added that this was the seventh time Israel struck the hospital in the past couple of years.
 “The strike targeted the second floor of Nasser Medical Complex … This is one of the largest hospitals in the Gaza Strip and the only hospital still standing in Khan Younis, serving at least 500,000 people in southern Gaza,” Khoudary said.
 The Israeli military claimed it was targeting a Hamas member at the hospital.
 Hamas condemned the strike as a “war crime that exposes the [Israeli] occupation’s impunity”. In a statement it said: “Mediators and the US administration must take action to halt the occupation’s ongoing violations and ensure its adherence to a ceasefire.”
 Israel has continued near-daily attacks despite a so-called “ceasefire” that has been in place since October 2025. Since then, at least 1,600 Palestinians ⁠have been killed in Israeli attacks, Gaza’s health ministry says.
 Advertisement Before the strike on Nasser Medical Complex, Israeli attacks killed seven other Palestinians across the Strip.
 An Israeli air attack on Wednesday killed 38-year-old Mohammed Salem al-Daash in the Sabra neighbourhood, south of Gaza City.
 Another Palestinian was shot and killed by Israeli forces east of the Bureij camp in central Gaza, and another was killed in an Israeli drone strike in the Nassr neighbourhood, northwest of Gaza City.
 At least two Palestinians were killed and several others wounded in a strike that hit a tent sheltering displaced people in the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood, north of Gaza City.
 Al Jazeera’s Khoudary described the Israeli attacks as the indiscriminate targeting of civilians, saying people who were carrying on with simple attempts to survive lost their lives, such as “a man filling up a water tank, [who] was killed in a drone strike”.
 “In another attack, two brothers from the al-Absi family were killed while they were sheltering inside their tent on al-Jalaa Street,” she said, adding that nowhere in Gaza was safe.
 Ahmed Nabhan embraces the shrouded body of his daughter Maryam, 4, who was killed in a deadly sand embankment collapse at a camp for displaced Palestinians in Deir el-Balah, in the central Gaza Strip on November 9, 2026 [File: Eyad Baba/AFP] ‘Not an acceptable excuse’
 The Israeli attacks came as the UN appealed for more tents to be sent to the enclave because at least 70,000 tents were flooded in weekend rains, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office.
 Heavy rain has directly affected at least 106,000 people in Gaza in recent days, according to the UN children’s agency, UNICEF, with thousands of tents for displaced Palestinians submerged under water and latrines overflowing into camps.
 NGOs and local organisations say they do not have the resources or capacity to deal with the crisis, as Israel continues to restrict the entry of essential aid.
 “Ultimately, we need the Israeli authorities to cooperate with giving the permissions so that we can bring those tents in,” UN deputy spokesperson Farhan Haq told reporters at a media briefing, adding that apart from funding, Israeli permits were needed “to get this in”.
 Certain countries supporting aid deliveries to Gaza have said that delivering winter supplies will have to wait for the formation of an Israeli government, according to Tom Fletcher, the UN under-secretary-general for humanitarian affairs.
 In a statement, Fletcher said foreign ministers have assured their support, “but also repeatedly said that progress would be hard until after Israeli elections. Now we’re told to wait for the formation of a government.
 Advertisement “This is not an acceptable excuse,” he added, citing international law and the consequences of delays, blockages and funding cuts.
 Italy’s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on Wednesday that Rome has launched a new emergency initiative worth 5 million euros ($5.5m) to provide immediate assistance to the Gaza Strip following the floods.
 The death toll from Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza has surged to 74,653 civilians killed since October 7, 2023, according to health authorities in Gaza.
 An additional 176,007 Palestinians have been injured in the past three years. More than 5,878 people have been injured since the Gaza “ceasefire” agreement came into effect in October 2025.
